items.labelFr: Délai de transmission d'une synapse rapide
items.conditions: Time from the start of the action potential in the sending nerve ending to the start of the response in the receiving neuron. Rat cerebellar synapses, measured at physiological (body) temperature.
items.conditionsFr: Temps entre le début de l'influx dans la terminaison nerveuse émettrice et le début de la réponse du neurone récepteur. Synapses du cervelet de rat, mesurées à température physiologique (celle du corps).
items.quote: postsynaptic responses commence just 150 micros after the start of the presynaptic action potential
items.confidenceNotes: Measured in rat brain slices, not in humans. The original uses the microsecond symbol; the Europe PMC rendering shows it as 'micros'. It is slower at room temperature, per the same abstract. Other synapse types are slower. Read from the abstract only. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: value restated from the source abstract or summary; no protocol written here: classified documented.

items.conditions: Approximate time for the whole voltage spike of a neuron, from depolarization back to resting potential (textbook description of a typical neuron).
items.conditionsFr: Durée approximative du pic électrique complet d'un neurone, de la dépolarisation au retour au potentiel de repos (description de manuel pour un neurone typique).
items.locator: Section 'The Action Potential', paragraph before 'refractory period' (refers to Figure 12.24)
items.quote: All of this takes place within approximately 2 milliseconds
items.era: Anatomy and Physiology 2e (OpenStax); publication year not checked on the page
items.confidenceNotes: Textbook order of magnitude for a typical neuron. Real durations vary by cell type. No primary measurement is cited at this spot.

items.labelEn: A quick eye jump while reading (saccade)
items.labelFr: Un saut rapide de l'œil pendant la lecture (saccade)
items.conditions: Duration of one saccade, the jump of the eyes from one point to the next, during reading. The range is the typical span for reading. Saccades in general last about 20-200 ms depending on their size.
items.conditionsFr: Durée d'une saccade (saut du regard d'un point à un autre) pendant la lecture. La fourchette est l'intervalle typique en lecture. Une saccade en général dure environ 20 à 200 ms selon son amplitude.
items.locator: Article body, paragraph on peak angular speed and saccade timing, revision 1374500057 (section heading not recorded)
items.quote: last from about 20–200 ms, depending on their amplitude (20–30 ms is typical in language reading)
items.confidenceNotes: Wikipedia is a tertiary source, used as a last resort. The primary references behind it were not traced. The central value is the midpoint of the source's range, not a value stated by the source. Harwood et al. 1999 (J Neurosci, PMC6782780) only says saccades are 'usually completed in tens of milliseconds', which is consistent. Replace with a primary main-sequence source if one can be opened (e.g. Purves, Neuroscience, NCBI Bookshelf NBK10991). | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: typical value = middle of the range published by the source; shown as illustrative with that range.

items.labelEn: Time between two heartbeats at rest (adult)
items.labelFr: Intervalle entre deux battements de cœur au repos (adulte)
items.conditions: Resting adult. Calculated from the normal resting heart rate range of 60-100 beats per minute: 100 bpm gives 0.6 s and 60 bpm gives 1 s.
items.conditionsFr: Adulte au repos. Calculé à partir de la fréquence cardiaque normale au repos (60 à 100 battements par minute) : 100 bpm donnent 0,6 s, 60 bpm donnent 1 s.
items.locator: Section 'Heart Rates', box 'Disorders of the... Heart: Abnormal Heart Rates'
items.quote: For an adult, normal resting HR will be in the range of 60–100 bpm.
items.era: Anatomy and Physiology 2e (OpenStax); publication year not checked on the page
items.confidenceNotes: The 60-100 bpm range is the textbook definition of a normal adult resting rate (below 60 is bradycardia, above 100 tachycardia, same page). Newborn resting rates may be 120 bpm (same page). The 0.75 s central value is the midpoint of the range, not a measured mean. MedlinePlus gives the same range but its ADAM content forbids AI reuse, so it was not used. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: typical value = middle of the range published by the source; shown as illustrative with that range.

items.labelEn: Time for one breath at rest (adult)
items.conditions: Resting adult or adolescent. Calculated from the normal resting rate of 12-18 breaths per minute: 18/min gives about 3.3 s per breath and 12/min gives 5 s.
items.conditionsFr: Adulte ou adolescent au repos. Calculé à partir de la fréquence respiratoire normale au repos (12 à 18 respirations par minute) : 18/min donnent environ 3,3 s par respiration, 12/min donnent 5 s.
items.locator: Section 'Respiratory Rate and Control of Ventilation'
items.quote: By adolescence, the normal respiratory rate is similar to that of adults, 12 to 18 breaths per minute.
items.era: Anatomy and Physiology 2e (OpenStax); publication year not checked on the page
items.confidenceNotes: Textbook reference range. Infants breathe 30-60 times per minute (same page). The central value is the midpoint of the range, not a measured mean. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: typical value = middle of the range published by the source; shown as illustrative with that range.

items.labelEn: Adult life of the shortest-lived mayfly (female Dolania americana)
items.labelFr: Vie adulte de l'éphémère la plus brève (femelle de Dolania americana)
items.conditions: Time a female of the mayfly Dolania americana lives after its final molt, during which it mates and lays eggs. The value is an upper bound ('less than five minutes'). Most mayfly species live at most about 48 hours as adults.
items.conditionsFr: Temps que vit la femelle de l'éphémère Dolania americana après sa dernière mue ; elle s'accouple et pond pendant ce temps. La valeur est une borne haute (« moins de cinq minutes »). La plupart des éphémères vivent au plus environ 48 heures à l'état adulte.
items.locator: Introduction (first paragraph); repeated in Results and Discussion
items.quote: the female of the mayfly Dolania americana (Ephemeroptera) which lives for less than five minutes after its final molt
items.confidenceNotes: Secondary compilation. The primary study (Sweeney & Vannote 1982) was not opened. This is an extreme case, not a typical mayfly. Same chapter: 'few species live more than 48 hours as adults'. Read from an archived snapshot.

items.labelEn: E. coli doubling time in the lab (best conditions)
items.labelFr: Temps de doublement d'E. coli au laboratoire (conditions optimales)
items.conditions: Escherichia coli in the laboratory, with oxygen and rich nutrients: the time for one cell to divide into two.
items.conditionsFr: Escherichia coli au laboratoire, avec oxygène et nutriments abondants : temps pour qu'une cellule se divise en deux.
items.locator: Section 1. Introduction, first sentence; also Table 1 (laboratory DT 0.33 h)
items.quote: The bacterium Escherichia coli can divide every 20 min in the laboratory under aerobic, nutrient-rich conditions.
items.confidenceNotes: A widely cited textbook figure stated in a peer-reviewed open-access paper. The value depends on strain, medium and temperature (usually 37 °C, not stated here). Gibson et al. give it as background, not as their own measurement.

items.labelEn: E. coli doubling time in the wild (gut), estimated
items.labelFr: Temps de doublement d'E. coli dans la nature (intestin), estimé
items.conditions: Estimated average time between divisions for E. coli in its natural environment, inferred indirectly from how fast mutations accumulate in the wild compared with the lab. Standard error 7.7 h (Table 1).
items.conditionsFr: Temps moyen estimé entre deux divisions d'E. coli dans son milieu naturel, déduit indirectement de la vitesse d'accumulation des mutations dans la nature comparée au laboratoire. Erreur type 7,7 h (tableau 1).
items.locator: Results text immediately before Table 1; Table 1 (E. coli DT 15 h, s.e. 7.7)
items.quote: E. coli can double every 20 min in the laboratory but we estimate that it only doubles every 15 h in the wild
items.confidenceNotes: Model-based estimate with large uncertainty (s.e. 7.7 h). It assumes the mutation rate per generation is the same in the wild and the lab. Useful as a contrast with the 20 min lab value.

items.labelFr: Un cycle de sommeil (sommeil lent + paradoxal)
items.conditions: Length of one cycle through the non-REM and REM sleep phases in a night's sleep. The range is the span the source gives. Usually there are four to six cycles per night.
items.conditionsFr: Durée d'un cycle complet entre sommeil lent (non-REM) et sommeil paradoxal (REM) au cours d'une nuit. La fourchette est celle donnée par la source ; il y a d'habitude quatre à six cycles par nuit.
items.locator: Page 'Sleep Phases and Stages', introductory paragraph (before 'Non-REM sleep')
items.quote: The cycle starts over every 80 to 100 minutes. Usually there are four to six cycles per night.
items.confidenceNotes: Patient-education page from a federal agency, with no primary study cited. The 90 min central value is the midpoint of the source's range, not stated as such by the source. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: typical value = middle of the range published by the source; shown as illustrative with that range.

items.labelEn: Natural period of the human body clock
items.labelFr: Période naturelle de l'horloge biologique humaine
items.conditions: Intrinsic period of the human circadian pacemaker, measured under a forced-desynchrony protocol that separates the body clock from the light-dark cycle. Average for healthy young and older adults.
items.conditionsFr: Période intrinsèque de l'horloge circadienne humaine, mesurée selon un protocole de « désynchronisation forcée » qui sépare l'horloge interne du cycle jour-nuit. Moyenne chez des adultes sains jeunes et âgés.
items.quote: the intrinsic period of the human circadian pacemaker averages 24.18 hours in both age groups
items.confidenceNotes: Landmark controlled lab study. The number of subjects and the spread between individuals are not in the abstract and were not read (full text paywalled), so low/high stay null. Older free-running studies reported ~25 h, a figure the same abstract presents as superseded. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: value restated from the source abstract or summary; no protocol written here: classified documented.

items.labelEn: Lifespan of a human red blood cell
items.labelFr: Durée de vie d'un globule rouge humain
items.conditions: Mean time a red blood cell circulates in a healthy person before removal. The range is the variation between individual cells around that mean.
items.conditionsFr: Temps moyen pendant lequel un globule rouge circule chez une personne en bonne santé avant d'être éliminé. La fourchette décrit la variation entre cellules individuelles autour de cette moyenne.
items.quote: In a normal individual with a mean RBC lifespan of 115 days, this value may vary between 70 and 140 days
items.confidenceNotes: Peer-reviewed review by a specialist in RBC survival measurement (biotin and 51Cr labelling). The textbook figure is 120 days: OpenStax A&P 2e 18.3 says 'Erythrocytes live up to 120 days in the circulation', which is consistent. Quote was extracted by WebFetch with citation markers removed.

items.labelEn: Length of a human pregnancy (from ovulation to birth)
items.labelFr: Durée d'une grossesse humaine (de l'ovulation à la naissance)
items.conditions: Median time from ovulation (conception) to birth in 125 naturally conceived single-baby pregnancies (US cohort, 1982-85). Even without preterm births, lengths spread over a 37-day range. Measured from ovulation, not from the last menstrual period as usually done in clinics.
items.conditionsFr: Durée médiane entre l'ovulation (conception) et la naissance pour 125 grossesses uniques conçues naturellement (cohorte américaine, 1982-85). Même sans les naissances prématurées, les durées s'étalent sur 37 jours. Mesurée depuis l'ovulation, et non depuis les dernières règles comme on le fait d'habitude en clinique.
items.locator: Abstract, 'Main results and the role of chance'
items.quote: The median time from ovulation to birth was 268 days (38 weeks, 2 days).
items.confidenceNotes: Ovulation was dated with urinary hormones, a gold-standard method, but the sample is small (n=125). The source states a 37-day spread, not explicit bounds, so low/high are null. The abstract notes that dating by last menstrual period gives more variation (CV 4.9% vs 3.7%). | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: value restated from the source abstract or summary; no protocol written here: classified documented.

items.labelEn: Life cycle of periodical cicadas (17-year broods)
items.labelFr: Cycle de vie des cigales périodiques (couvées de 17 ans)
items.conditions: Interval between mass emergences of Magicicada periodical cicadas at a given place in the eastern United States. Broods come out every 13 or every 17 years; the value is the 17-year type and 'low' is the 13-year type (two fixed cycle lengths, not a continuous range).
items.conditionsFr: Intervalle entre deux émergences massives des cigales périodiques Magicicada en un même lieu de l'est des États-Unis. Les couvées sortent tous les 13 ou tous les 17 ans ; la valeur correspond au type à 17 ans et « low » au type à 13 ans (deux durées fixes, pas une plage continue).
items.quote: These year classes ("broods") emerge dependably every 13 or 17 yr in a given location.
items.confidenceNotes: Well established. The same abstract notes that a sizeable part of a population sometimes emerges 4 years early or late. The low/high pair stands for two discrete cycle types. Split it into two items if the atlas model needs that. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: 13 and 17 years are two distinct cycle types, not a range: value 17 years (17-year broods), low/high left null.

items.labelFr: Fréquence des battements d'ailes de l'abeille (vol stationnaire)
items.conditions: Wingbeat frequency of honeybees while hovering, measured in the lab. That is about 230 wing strokes per second (about 4.3 ms per stroke, my conversion).
items.conditionsFr: Fréquence des battements d'ailes d'abeilles en vol stationnaire, mesurée au laboratoire : environ 230 battements par seconde (soit à peu près 4,3 ms par battement, conversion de ma part).
items.quote: hovering with relatively low stroke amplitude (approximately 90 degrees) and high wingbeat frequency (approximately 230 Hz)
items.confidenceNotes: Peer-reviewed measurement, stated as approximate. Read from the abstract only, so the measurement method was not checked. The 4.3 ms per stroke figure is 1/230 s, computed by me. Frequency varies with temperature, load and individual. Per the abstract it stayed nearly constant in low-density heliox. | Maintainer curation 2026-11-27: value restated from the source abstract or summary; no protocol written here: classified documented.

items.labelEn: Life expectancy at birth, United States, 2024
items.labelFr: Espérance de vie à la naissance, États-Unis, 2024
items.conditions: Life expectancy at birth for both sexes in the United States in 2024 (males 76.5 years, females 81.4 years), as published by NCHS. A statistical average, not a prediction for any one person.
items.conditionsFr: Espérance de vie à la naissance (tous sexes) aux États-Unis en 2024 (hommes 76,5 ans, femmes 81,4 ans), publiée par le NCHS. Moyenne statistique, pas une prévision individuelle.
items.locator: Section 'Life Expectancy', bullet 'Life expectancy at birth'
items.confidenceNotes: Official national statistic computed by NCHS from life tables. The underlying data brief (db548) was not opened. Varies strongly by country and year. A WHO global figure was not sourced.
